items.label: Setup S-1
items.nl: Independent sampling of \(n\) observed records \(O_i=(X_i,A_i,Y_i)\in[d]\times\{0,1\}^2\) from a finite observed law, described by its cell four-mass vectors \(q_j\in\mathbb R_+^4\), with cell masses \(p_j\), propensities \(e_j\), fixed overlap constant \(\epsilon\in(0,1/2)\), budget interval \(I=[b_0,1-b_0]\), shadow price \(\lambda\in[0,1]\), threshold cell functional \(f_\lambda(u)\) built from \(s_a(u),s(u),g_a(u)\), dual process \(F_P(\lambda)\), and the Jackson--factorial estimator with tuning \(H_0=4096,\kappa=1/512,D_0=16\).

items.label: Setup S-2
items.nl: A full-data causal law \(P\) of \((X,A,Y(0),Y(1))\) on \([d]\times\{0,1\}^3\) with observed outcome \(Y\), cell potential-outcome means \(\mu_{aj}\), effects \(\tau_j\), control value \(B(P)\), randomized policies \(\pi\in[0,1]^d\), budget-feasible class \(\Pi_b(P)\), oracle value \(V_b(P)\) and curve \(V(P)\), model class \(\mathcal M_{d,\epsilon}\), and the all-procedure squared-supremum minimax risk \(\mathfrak R^{\mathrm{curve}}_{n,d,\epsilon,b_0}\).

items.label: Setup S-3
items.nl: The paired lower-bound experiment: \(k\) cell pairs indexed by \(i\) and sign \(\sigma\in\{-1,+1\}\), pair masses \(r\in\Delta_k\), contrasts \(\theta\in[-1/8,1/8]^k\), the family \(\mathcal P^{\mathrm{pair}}_k\subset\mathcal M_{2k,\epsilon}\), and the normalized two-sample \(L_1\) experiment with \(n\) independent draws from each of \(R,S\in\Delta_k\).

items.label: Definition P-1
items.nl: \(\mathcal M_{d,\epsilon}=\{P: X\in[d],\ A,Y(0),Y(1)\in\{0,1\},\ P\text{ satisfies }\mathrm{ass:consistency},\mathrm{ass:conditional\mbox{-}exchangeability},\mathrm{ass:overlap}\}\), for each integer \(d\ge2\).

items.label: Definition P-4
items.nl: For \(u\in\mathbb R_+^4\), set \(g_a(u)=s(u)u_{a1}/\max\{s_a(u),\epsilon s(u)\}\), with the quotient equal to zero when all four coordinates of \(u\) vanish; set \(f_\lambda(u)=g_0(u)+[g_1(u)-g_0(u)-\lambda s(u)]_+\) and \(F_P(\lambda)=\sum_{j=1}^d f_\lambda(q_j)\).

items.label: Definition P-5
items.nl: For \(b_0\in[0,1/2]\), let \(I=[b_0,1-b_0]\) and define \(\mathfrak R_{n,d,\epsilon,b_0}^{\mathrm{curve}}=\inf_{\widehat V}\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_{d,\epsilon}}E_P[\sup_{b\in I}|\widehat V_b(O^{(n)})-V_b(P)|^2]\), where the infimum is over all measurable maps into bounded functions on \(I\).

items.label: Definition P-6
items.nl:
Set \(H_0=4096\), \(\kappa=1/512\), \(D_0=16\), \(L=\log(ed)\), \(m=n/8\), and \(K=\max\{2,\lfloor L/512\rfloor\}\).  Write \(\mathcal Z=\{0,1\}^2\), with \(\zeta=(a,y)\).  If \(d<16\), set
\[
 \widehat q_{\zeta j}=\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n
 \mathbf 1\{X_i=j,(A_i,Y_i)=\zeta\},\qquad
 \widehat F(\lambda)=\sum_{j=1}^d f_\lambda(\widehat q_j).
\]
If \(d\geq16\) and \(n<d/L\), define \(\widehat V_b^{\mathrm{JF}}=1/2\) for every \(b\in I\).  In the remaining case \(d\geq16\) and \(n\geq d/L\), independently of \(O^{(n)}\), draw \(M\sim\operatorname{Pois}(n/4)\).  On \(\{M>n\}\), set the entire auxiliary threshold process \(\widetilde F^{\mathrm{cap}}(\lambda)=0\) for every \(\lambda\in[0,1]\).  On \(\{M\leq n\}\), uniformly permute the \(n\) records, retain the first \(M\), and independently mark each retained record pilot or evaluation with probability \(1/2\) each.  Let \(N'_{\zeta j}\) and \(N_{\zeta j}\) be the resulting pilot and evaluation counts.

For each \(j\) and \(\zeta\), put
\[
 \delta=\frac Lm,\quad c_{\zeta j}=\frac{N'_{\zeta j}}m,\quad
 h_{\zeta j}=4096\{\sqrt{c_{\zeta j}\delta}+\delta\},
\]
\[
 \ell_{\zeta j}=\max\{0,c_{\zeta j}-h_{\zeta j}\},\quad
 u_{\zeta j}=c_{\zeta j}+h_{\zeta j},\quad
 c^0_{\zeta j}=\frac{\ell_{\zeta j}+u_{\zeta j}}2,\quad
 R_{\zeta j}=\frac{u_{\zeta j}-\ell_{\zeta j}}2,
 \quad S_j=\sum_{\zeta\in\mathcal Z}R_{\zeta j}.
\]
All radii are strictly positive.  Define the normalized positive order-four Jackson kernel
\[
 J_K(t)=C_K\left\{\frac{\sin(Kt/2)}{\sin(t/2)}\right\}^{4},
 \qquad -\pi\leq t\leq\pi,qquad
 \int_{-\pi}^{\pi}J_K(t)\,dt=1,
\]
where the quotient has its continuous value at zero and \(C_K\) is the unique positive normalizing constant.  With \(D=2(K-1)\), define the unique tensor polynomial \(P_{j,\lambda}\), of coordinatewise degree at most \(D\), by
\[
 P_{j,\lambda}(c_j^0+R_j\odot\cos\vartheta)
 =\int_{[-\pi,\pi]^4}
 f_\lambda(c_j^0+R_j\odot\cos(\vartheta+t))
 \prod_{\zeta\in\mathcal Z}J_K(t_\zeta)\,dt,
\]
and take its unique monomial expansion
\[
 P_{j,\lambda}(u)-f_\lambda(c_j^0)
 =\sum_{\alpha\in\{0,\ldots,D\}^4}
 \beta_{j,\alpha}(\lambda)
 \prod_{\zeta\in\mathcal Z}
 \left(\frac{u_\zeta-c^0_{\zeta j}}{R_{\zeta j}}\right)^{\alpha_\zeta}.
\]
For \(h\geq0\), set
\[
 U_h(N;z)=\sum_{t=0}^h {h\choose t}(-z)^{h-t}\frac{(N)_t}{m^t},
 \qquad (N)_t=N(N-1)\cdots(N-t+1),\qquad (N)_0=1,
\]
and define
\[
 Z_j(\lambda)=f_\lambda(c_j^0)+
 \sum_{\alpha\in\{0,\ldots,D\}^4}\beta_{j,\alpha}(\lambda)
 \prod_{\zeta\in\mathcal Z}
 \frac{U_{\alpha_\zeta}(N_{\zeta j};c^0_{\zeta j})}
 {R_{\zeta j}^{\alpha_\zeta}},
\]
\[
 T_j(\lambda)=f_\lambda(c_j^0)+
 \Pi_{[-d^{1/4}S_j,d^{1/4}S_j]}
 \{Z_j(\lambda)-f_\lambda(c_j^0)\},
 \qquad
 \widetilde F^{\mathrm{cap}}(\lambda)=\sum_{j=1}^dT_j(\lambda)
 \quad\text{on }\{M\leq n\}.
\]
Here \(\Pi_{[r,s]}(x)=\min\{s,\max\{r,x\}\}\).  In the Jackson--factorial branch, average the threshold process before performing the dual minimization:
\[
 \widehat F(\lambda)=E\{\widetilde F^{\mathrm{cap}}(\lambda)\mid O^{(n)}\}.
\]
In both the empirical and Jackson--factorial branches, report
\[
 \widehat V_b^{\mathrm{JF}}
 =\Pi_{[0,1]}\left(\min_{0\leq\lambda\leq1}
 \{b\lambda+\widehat F(\lambda)\}\right),\qquad b\in I.
\]
The reported quantity is the minimum value and therefore requires no optimizer selection.  If an implementation stores an optimizer, it stores the least element of the nonempty compact argmin set.  These branch rules, the zero process on \(\{M>n\}\), and the least-minimizer convention apply also under every data or treatment-effect tie.

items.label: Definition P-7
items.nl:
For fixed \(0<\epsilon<1/2\), the common-polynomial process handle \(\mathsf H_\epsilon\) for the single pilot-local Jackson polynomial and clipping rule in \(\widehat V^{\mathrm{JF}}\) is the set of candidate constants \(C>0\). Membership requires the following five groups of bounds simultaneously for every \(n,d\) in the Jackson--factorial branch, every observed categorical law \(P\) on the known \(d\)-cell alphabet, every pilot realization, every cell \(j\), and every \(\lambda\in[0,1]\). Thus the definition gives a uniform membership criterion; it does not assert that a candidate exists. Nonemptiness is proved in \(\mathrm{thm:integrated\mbox{-}process\mbox{-}certificate}\), which chooses one \(C_\epsilon\) depending only on \(\epsilon\).

Set \(L=\log(ed)\), \(m=n/8\), \(K=\max\{2,\lfloor L/512\rfloor\}\), \(S_j=\sum_{\zeta\in\mathcal Z}R_{\zeta j}\), and \(v_j=\sqrt{p_jL/m}+L/m\). For all expectations and \(L_2\) norms in these five groups, use the ideal uncapped marked--Poisson experiment of proof (1), in which the pilot and evaluation counts \(N'_{\zeta j},N_{\zeta j}\sim\operatorname{Pois}(m q_{\zeta j})\) are mutually independent; the executable capped experiment is used only in the final transfer to \(\widetilde F^{\mathrm{cap}}\). Define the quarter-halfwidth pilot event by \(G_j=\bigcap_{\zeta\in\mathcal Z}\{|c_{\zeta j}-q_{\zeta j}|\leq h_{\zeta j}/4\}\), and use the convention \(\|h\|_{BV([0,1])}=|h(0)|+\operatorname{TV}_{[0,1]}(h)\). Use the clipped path \(T_j\), coefficient array \(\beta_{j,\alpha}\), and pilot radii \(R_{\zeta j}\) from the estimator, evaluated in that uncapped experiment. Membership of \(C\) means:
\[
\sum_\alpha\|\beta_{j,\alpha}\|_{BV([0,1])}\leq C S_j e^{12K},\qquad
S_j^2 e^{24K+16K^2/L}\leq C d^{1/16}S_j^2;
\]
\[
E\left\|\sum_{j=1}^d\left[\mathbf1_{G_j}\{T_j-f_\cdot(q_j)\}-E\mathbf1_{G_j}\{T_j-f_\cdot(q_j)\}\right]\right\|_\infty^2\leq C\frac d{mL};
\]
\[
\sup_{0\leq\lambda\leq1}|ET_j(\lambda)-f_\lambda(q_j)|\leq C\left\{\sqrt{\frac{p_j}{mL}}+\frac1{mL}\right\};
\]
\[
\left\|\mathbf1_{G_j^c}\sup_{0\leq\lambda\leq1}|T_j(\lambda)-f_\lambda(q_j)|\right\|_{L_2}\leq C d^{1/4}e^{-10L}v_j;
\]
\[
E\left\|\sum_{j=1}^d\left[\mathbf1_{G_j^c}\{T_j-f_\cdot(q_j)\}-E\mathbf1_{G_j^c}\{T_j-f_\cdot(q_j)\}\right]\right\|_\infty^2\leq C\frac d{mL}.
\]
The first group is the coefficient envelope (14) and deterministic exponential absorption (20), obtained in the proof using the conditional factorial moment (19); the remaining groups are proof (33), (27), (28), and (34). The two bad-pilot groups are distinct: (28) is an uncentered per-cell \(L_2\) supremum envelope, whereas (34) is a centered aggregate squared risk. The handle uses the same polynomial and numerical tuning as the estimator and targets the shadow-price process formed by summing cellwise errors relative to \(f_\lambda(q_j)\).

items.label: Definition P-8
items.nl: For \(k\ge1\), choose \(r=(r_1,\ldots,r_k)\) in the simplex and \(\theta_i\in[-1/8,1/8]\). Create cells \((i,+),(i,-)\) of masses \(r_i/2\), set \(e_{i,\sigma}=1/2\), \(\mu_{0,i,\sigma}=1/4\), and \(\mu_{1,i,\sigma}=1/2+\sigma\theta_i\). The family of causal completions generated independently of \(A\) given \(X\) is \(\mathcal P^{\mathrm{pair}}_k\).

items.label: Assumption A-1
items.nl: The records \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\) are independent and identically distributed under the observed margin of \(P\).

items.label: Lemma L-1
items.nl: There is \(C_\epsilon<\infty\) such that for all \(u,v\in\mathbb R_+^4\), \(\|f_{\cdot}(u)-f_{\cdot}(v)\|_{BV([0,1])}\le C_\epsilon\|u-v\|_1\), where \(\|h\|_{BV}=|h(0)|+\operatorname{TV}_{[0,1]}(h)\).

items.label: Lemma L-2
items.nl:
There is a universal constant \(c>0\) such that, for every \(k\geq2\) and \(1\leq n\leq k^2\), the experiment consisting of \(n\) independent observations from each of \(R,S\in\Delta_k\) satisfies
\[
 \inf_{\widehat L}\sup_{R,S\in\Delta_k}
 E_{R,S}\bigl[(\widehat L-\|R-S\|_1)^2\bigr]
 \geq c\min\left\{1,\frac{k}{n\log(ek)}\right\}.
\]

items.label: Lemma lem:empirical-threshold-process-bounded
items.nl: Let \(\epsilon\in\mathbb R\), \(n,d\in\mathbb N\), and fix any observed sample \(O^{(n)}\). The empirical threshold process of \cref{obj:def:jf-estimator}, \(\widehat F(\lambda)=\sum_{j=1}^d f_\lambda(\widehat q_j)\) with \(f_\lambda\) as in \cref{obj:def:dual-process}, is bounded on \([0,1]\): there is a finite \(B\) (depending on the sample) such that \(|\widehat F(\lambda)|\leq B\) for every \(\lambda\in[0,1]\).

items.label: Lemma lem:averaged-threshold-process-bounded
items.nl: Let \(\epsilon>0\), \(n\geq1\), and \(d\geq1\), and fix any observed sample \(O^{(n)}\). The conditionally averaged threshold process of \cref{obj:def:jf-estimator}, obtained by averaging the capped auxiliary process \(\widetilde F^{\mathrm{cap}}(\lambda)\) over \(M\sim\operatorname{Pois}(n/4)\), the uniform record permutation, and the pilot/evaluation marks given \(O^{(n)}\), is bounded on \([0,1]\): there is a finite \(B\) (depending on the sample) such that \(|\widehat F(\lambda)|\leq B\) for every \(\lambda\in[0,1]\).

items.label: Lemma lem:pilot-radius-second-moment
items.nl:
Let \(n\geq1\), \(d\geq16\), \(m=n/8\), \(L=\log(ed)\), \(H_0=4096\), let \(P\) be an observed categorical law on the \(d\)-cell alphabet with category-cell masses \(q_{\zeta j}\) and cell masses \(p_j=\sum_{\zeta\in\mathcal Z}q_{\zeta j}\), and fix a cell \(j\). In the ideal uncapped experiment in which the pilot counts \(N'_{\zeta j}\sim\operatorname{Pois}(mq_{\zeta j})\) are independent, let \(S_j=\sum_{\zeta\in\mathcal Z}R_{\zeta j}\) be the sum of the four pilot radii of \cref{obj:def:jf-estimator}, and let \(v_j=\sqrt{p_jL/m}+L/m\) as in \cref{obj:def:process-handle}. Then \(S_j^2\) is integrable and
\[
\mathbb E\,S_j^2\leq 32H_0^2\,v_j^2 .
\]

items.label: Lemma lem:jackson-boundary-adaptive
Lemma lem:pilot-bad-score-moment
items.nl:
Let \(n\geq1\), \(d\geq1\), \(m=n/8\), \(L=\log(ed)\), and \(H_0=4096\). Let \(P\) be an observed categorical law on the \(d\)-cell alphabet with category-cell masses \(q_{\zeta j}\) and cell masses \(p_j=\sum_{\zeta\in\mathcal Z}q_{\zeta j}\), and fix a cell \(j\). Suppose the four pilot counts \(N'_{\zeta j}\), \(\zeta\in\mathcal Z\), are independent with \(N'_{\zeta j}\sim\operatorname{Pois}(mq_{\zeta j})\). Form \(c_{\zeta j}\) and \(h_{\zeta j}\) from these counts as in \cref{obj:def:jf-estimator}, let \(G_j\) be the quarter-halfwidth pilot event and \(v_j=\sqrt{p_jL/m}+L/m\) the pilot-error scale of \cref{obj:def:process-handle}, and put
\[
B_j=\sum_{\zeta\in\mathcal Z}\bigl(|c_{\zeta j}-q_{\zeta j}|+h_{\zeta j}\bigr).
\]
Then, for each \(t\in\{1,2,4\}\),
\[
\mathbb E\bigl[\mathbf 1_{G_j^c}B_j^{\,t}\bigr]
\leq4^t\,10^{80(t+1)}\,e^{-20L}\,v_j^{\,t}.
\]

items.label: Lemma lem:bv-maximal-cell-paths
items.nl:
Let \(n,d\geq1\), \(\epsilon>0\), and let \(P\) be an observed categorical law on the \(d\)-cell alphabet with category-cell masses \(q_{\zeta j}\). Work in the ideal experiment of \cref{obj:def:process-handle}, in which all pilot and evaluation counts \(N'_{\zeta j}\) and \(N_{\zeta j}\) are mutually independent with \(\operatorname{Pois}(mq_{\zeta j})\) laws, \(m=n/8\). Fix one of the two pilot events: either \(E_j=G_j\) for every cell \(j\), or \(E_j=G_j^c\) for every cell \(j\), with \(G_j\) as in \cref{obj:def:process-handle}. For each cell \(j\), let \(W_j(\lambda)=\mathbf1_{E_j}\{T_j(\lambda)-f_\lambda(q_j)\}\), \(\lambda\in[0,1]\), where \(T_j\) is the clipped cell estimate of \cref{obj:def:jf-estimator} and \(f_\lambda\) is as in \cref{obj:def:dual-process}. Assume that each \(W_j\) is continuous in \(\lambda\) for every count table; that each map from count tables to \(W_j\in C([0,1])\) is measurable and Bochner integrable; that each \(W_j\) has almost surely finite total variation \(\operatorname{TV}_{[0,1]}(W_j)\); that \((\|W_j\|_\infty+\operatorname{TV}_{[0,1]}(W_j))^2\) is integrable; and that the paths \(W_1,\ldots,W_d\) are independent. Then
\[
\mathbb E\left\|\sum_{j=1}^d\bigl(W_j-\mathbb EW_j\bigr)\right\|_\infty^2
\leq16384\sum_{j=1}^d\mathbb E\Bigl[\bigl(\|W_j\|_\infty+\operatorname{TV}_{[0,1]}(W_j)\bigr)^2\Bigr].
\]

items.label: Lemma lem:capped-marked-count-identity
items.nl:
Let \(n,d\geq1\) and \(m=n/8\), and let \(P\) be an observed categorical law on the \(d\)-cell alphabet with category-cell masses \(q_{\zeta j}\). For a sample \(O^{(n)}=(O_1,\ldots,O_n)\), a permutation \(\sigma\) of \(\{1,\ldots,n\}\), an integer \(0\leq M\leq n\), and marks \(\omega\in\{\mathrm{pilot},\mathrm{evaluation}\}^n\), let \((N',N)=(N'_{\zeta j},N_{\zeta j})_{\zeta,j}\) be the pilot and evaluation count table of the first \(M\) permuted records \(O_{\sigma(1)},\ldots,O_{\sigma(M)}\), where the \(i\)-th permuted record is counted as pilot or evaluation according to \(\omega_i\), as in \cref{obj:def:jf-estimator}; the marks \(\omega_{M+1},\ldots,\omega_n\) do not affect the table. Put \(w_n(M)=\Pr\{\operatorname{Pois}(n/4)=M\}/(n!\,2^n)\). Consider the uncapped marked-Poisson experiment: draw \(M\sim\operatorname{Pois}(n/4)\), then \(M\) independent records from \(P\), each marked pilot or evaluation independently with probability \(1/2\), and let \((N',N)\) be the resulting count table. Then, for every real function \(g\) of count tables that is integrable under the ideal law of \cref{obj:def:process-handle}, in which all \(N'_{\zeta j}\) and \(N_{\zeta j}\) are independent \(\operatorname{Pois}(mq_{\zeta j})\),
\[
\mathbb E_{O^{(n)}\sim P^{\otimes n}}\left[\sum_{M=0}^{n}\sum_{\sigma}\sum_{\omega\in\{\mathrm{pilot},\mathrm{evaluation}\}^n}w_n(M)\,g\bigl(N'(O^{(n)},\sigma,M,\omega),N(O^{(n)},\sigma,M,\omega)\bigr)\right]
=\mathbb E_{\mathrm{uncapped}}\bigl[\mathbf1\{M\leq n\}\,g(N',N)\bigr].
\]

items.label: Theorem T-1
items.nl: For every \(P\in\mathcal M_{d,\epsilon}\) and \(b\in[0,1]\), \(V_b(P)=\inf_{0\le\lambda\le1}\{b\lambda+F_P(\lambda)\}\). Consequently, for any bounded process \(\widehat F\), \(\sup_{b\in[0,1]}|\inf_\lambda\{b\lambda+\widehat F(\lambda)\}-V_b(P)|\le\sup_{\lambda\in[0,1]}|\widehat F(\lambda)-F_P(\lambda)|\).

items.label: Theorem T-2
items.nl: With \(H_0=4096\), \(\kappa=1/512\), and \(D_0=16\), the handle \(\mathsf H_{n,d}\) is completed by the single positive order-four Jackson kernel and the clipping rule in \(\widehat V^{\mathrm{JF}}\). For each fixed \(0<\epsilon<1/2\), there exists one finite \(C_\epsilon>0\), depending only on \(\epsilon\), such that for every \(n,d\) in the Jackson--factorial branch, every \(P\in\mathcal M_{d,\epsilon}\), every cell \(j\), and every \(\lambda\in[0,1]\), the following bounds hold simultaneously: the cellwise scalar bias is at most \(C_\epsilon\{\sqrt{p_j/[n\log(ed)]}+1/[n\log(ed)]\}\), the good-pilot centered sum has expected squared supremum at most \(C_\epsilon d/[n\log(ed)]\); the uncentered cellwise bad-pilot envelope obeys \(\|\mathbf1_{G_j^c}\sup_{0\leq\lambda\leq1}|T_j(\lambda)-f_\lambda(q_j)|\|_{L_2}\leq C_\epsilon d^{1/4}e^{-10L}v_j\), and the centered aggregate bad-pilot risk obeys \(E\|\sum_{j=1}^d[\mathbf1_{G_j^c}\{T_j-f_\cdot(q_j)\}-E\mathbf1_{G_j^c}\{T_j-f_\cdot(q_j)\}]\|_\infty^2\leq C_\epsilon d/(mL)\), where \(L=\log(ed)\), \(m=n/8\), and \(v_j=\sqrt{p_jL/m}+L/m\). Consequently, in the Jackson--factorial branch, the dual threshold process constructed inside \(\widehat V^{\mathrm{JF}}\) has expected squared supremum distance from \(F_P\) at most \(C_\epsilon d/[n\log(ed)]\), with that same \(C_\epsilon\) uniform in \(n,d,P,j,\lambda\). These conclusions include null cells, boundary outcome means, and exact treatment-effect ties.

items.label: Theorem T-3
items.nl: Every law in \(\mathcal P^{\mathrm{pair}}_k\) belongs to \(\mathcal M_{2k,\epsilon}\), has every occupied-cell treatment effect in \([1/8,3/8]\) (that is, \(r_i>0\) implies \(1/8\leq\tau_{i,\sigma}\leq3/8\)), has the binding half-population budget with shadow price \(1/4\), satisfies \(V_{1/2}(P)=3/8+(1/2)\sum_{i=1}^k r_i|\theta_i|\), and has the known constant unrestricted value \(V_1(P)=1/2\). Moreover, for \(R,S\in\Delta_k\), the normalized embedding \(r_i=(R_i+S_i)/2\) and \(\theta_i=(R_i-S_i)/[8(R_i+S_i)]\), with zero assigned when the denominator vanishes, is generated by an exact fixed-sample Markov kernel from independent samples from \(R\) and \(S\).

items.label: Theorem T-4
items.nl: There is \(c_\epsilon>0\) such that for every \(n\geq1\) and \(d\geq2\), every estimator \(T\) obeys \(\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_{d,\epsilon}:\ V_1(P)=1/2,\ p_j>0\Rightarrow1/8\leq\tau_j\leq3/8}E_P[(T-V_{1/2}(P))^2]\ge c_\epsilon\min\{1,d/[n\log(ed)]\}\), with null-label padding allowed. The budget is binding throughout the hard family.

items.label: Theorem T-5
items.nl: There is \(C_{\epsilon}<\infty\) such that the total estimator \(\widehat V^{\mathrm{JF}}\) satisfies \(\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_{d,\epsilon}}E_P[\sup_{b\in I}|\widehat V_b^{\mathrm{JF}}-V_b(P)|^2]\le C_\epsilon\min\{1,d/[n\log(ed)]\}\) for every \(n\ge1\), \(d\ge2\), and \(b_0\in[0,1/2]\), uniformly over null cells, arbitrary occupied-cell masses, boundary outcome means, and exact treatment-effect ties.  When \(b_0=0\), the supremum covers the full budget curve on \([0,1]\).

items.label: Theorem T-6
items.nl: There exist \(0<c_\epsilon\le C_\epsilon<\infty\) such that for all \(n\ge1\), \(d\ge2\), and fixed \(b_0\in[0,1/2]\), \(c_\epsilon\min\{1,d/[n\log(ed)]\}\le\mathfrak R_{n,d,\epsilon,b_0}^{\mathrm{curve}}\le C_\epsilon\min\{1,d/[n\log(ed)]\}\).  The lower bound is witnessed at \(b=1/2\) by laws with positive occupied-cell effects, binding capacity, and known constant unrestricted value.  When \(b_0=0\), the risk concerns the full curve on \([0,1]\), whose \(b=1\) endpoint recovers the unrestricted scalar optimal-value target.

items.label: Theorem T-7
items.nl: For every fixed finite \(d\), the frontier in \(\mathrm{thm:matched\mbox{-}curve\mbox{-}frontier}\) reduces to squared risk of order \(n^{-1}\). If additionally \(\tau_j=c>0\) for every occupied cell, then \(V_b(P)=B(P)+cb\) for \(b\in I\), including exact ties, which is the known linear budget-value special case.

items.label: Cited result lem:jhw-known-q-l1-lower-regime
items.nl:
For every fixed \(a_0>0\) and \(C_0<\infty\), there are constants \(c_{a_0,C_0}>0\) and \(k_{a_0,C_0}<\infty\) such that, whenever \(k\geq k_{a_0,C_0}\), \(n\geq a_0 k/\log k\), and \(\log n\leq C_0\log k\), the experiment of \(n\) independent observations from \(R\in\Delta_k\), with \(S\in\Delta_k\) known to the estimator, satisfies
\[
 \sup_{S\in\Delta_k}\inf_{\widehat L_S}\sup_{R\in\Delta_k}
 E_R\!\left[(\widehat L_S-\|R-S\|_1)^2\right]
 \geq c_{a_0,C_0}\frac{k}{n\log n}.
\]
Here the infimum is over estimators based on the \(R\)-sample that may depend on the known distribution \(S\).

items.label: P
items.nl: realized by observedFromPotential, CanonicalObservedOutcome, PotentialLaw, variable@187
